Synopsis:
Indian equity markets (Nifty 50, BSE Sensex) posted a fifth consecutive weekly decline, down ~2% on the week and ~4.8% over five weeks. The primary driver is surging Brent crude (+8% to $104/bbl) fueled by escalating Middle East conflict — tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi threats to Saudi exports. Rising oil prices are stoking global inflation fears, pushing bond yields to multi-year highs. Broad-based sector weakness, a weakening rupee (-1% on the week), and pressure on IT stocks (anticipating a Fed rate hike) compound the bearish picture. US CPI data due Friday is the near-term catalyst watch ahead of next week's Fed decision.
